comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: RP-01 truncation clarification and correction to the preceding cache note. Current Rebar has three distinct behaviors: (1) source ticket/system/user/tool input is not truncated at this seam; plan review context overflow keeps full content, splits criteria/escalates model windows, then emits a decomposition failure rather than chunking content; (2) a provider response with finish_reason length/max_tokens/refusal/content_filter is rejected before repair as UnretryableOutputError and never accepted as a verdict; (3) only a failed intermediate response copied into a retry prompt is capped at 2,000 characters. The original failed response is parsed in full, accepted output is returned in full, and the optional final-failure artifact stores the complete final reply. Proposed same-run finding: Pydantic ProcessHistory is unsuitable because _agent_graph commits processed messages back into state. Offline probe: a 5,000-character failed response became 2,013 both on the retry wire and in result.all_messages(). A documented model_request wrapper is non-destructive: the provider still saw the same 2,013-character projection and 2,211-character retry request, while result.all_messages() retained all 5,000 characters. Live Anthropic and Bedrock reruns with this wrapper reproduced the prior cache counts exactly: agentic retry read/write 3,920/289, and stored assistant lengths included the full 5,000. Revised constraint: never truncate source inputs, tool evidence, accepted output, or stored raw responses; check provider truncation before repair and fail closed. Remaining maintainer choice: retain the existing 2,000-character retry-only projection through model_request, or intentionally remove it and send the full failed intermediate response back. Research note and recovery report updated; no production code changed.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: RP-01 D2 clarification: a truncated failed response on retry has correctness risk beyond extra recomputation. The discarded tail can contain valid material findings even when the overall JSON fails parsing/validation. A retry can then emit a schema-valid replacement containing only findings visible in the prefix; Pydantic validates shape, not completeness, so the omission may be silent. Concrete Rebar case: CompletionVerdict findings and legacy criteria both default to empty, and PASS with no findings is valid. Reconciliation can recover named failures from a populated criteria manifest but cannot recover findings omitted from both. Truncation can also remove the location relevant to the validation error and presents a counterfactual assistant turn. This reduces to work-only only if all material information is independently present in authoritative input and the model fully recomputes rather than edits the partial draft; Rebar cannot prove that generically. Common formatting-only failures are already repaired deterministically before retry, making the remaining failures a poor population for assuming the tail is irrelevant. Safe policy space is all-or-nothing: send the complete failed response when the complete operation fits, or fail closed / explicitly regenerate from complete authoritative inputs without presenting a partial response as history. Prefix truncation is not cost-only. Research note updated; D2 remains pending.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
RP-01 D2 approved and experimentally specified. Retry-wire policy: send the complete failed ModelResponse only when the complete retry deterministically fits; otherwise omit that response whole from a copied model_request context. Never prefix-truncate it and never mutate stored Agent history. Source/system/user/tool input, accepted output, and the final-failure artifact remain complete. Output-size policy is an intentional behavior change: length/max_tokens is rejected before parse/repair, then consumes the existing bounded output-retry allowance with the exact guidance “Make your response as concise as possible while fulfilling the prompt and output format requirements.” Refusal/content-filter remains terminal after one call and output-size failure still does not trigger provider fallback.

Fit rule: for every viable candidate, require a known Rebar context window and Pydantic count_tokens result for the full message/settings/request-parameter shape, then require input_tokens + effective max_tokens <= window. FallbackModel itself has no count_tokens implementation, so the capability iterates the already-built candidate models. Unknown window/count selects whole-response omission; count the omitted shape too and fail closed if authoritative inputs still cannot fit. Optional count calls do not consume Agent request_limit and are labeled separately in telemetry.

All-or-nothing branches sent respectively all 5,000 and zero failed-response characters on retry while both retained 5,000 in result.all_messages(); output-size→valid used 2 calls with the exact guidance; repeated output-size exhausted 3; content-filter/refusal used 1. ## Context
RP-01 proposes replacing Rebar’s bespoke structured-output orchestration with authoritative Pydantic AI seams. The replacement is not behavior-preserving by default: historical bugs encode hard-won behavior around deterministic repair and extraction, refusal/truncation handling, retry and tool/request limits, per-operation output budgets, provider fallback, usage accounting, telemetry, and failure taxonomy. Before RP-01 can be approved or ticketized, reconstruct the behavioral contract from both ticket history and the existing test suite and exercise the worktree virtualenv’s resolved Pydantic AI distribution. A behavior may be preserved or intentionally changed, but no observed delta may be accidental or left to the implementer.

The checkout-local probe path is `.joe-janitor/rp01-pydantic-native-probe.py`. The entire `.joe-janitor/` archive is intentionally excluded from repository snapshots, so an attested-source reviewer cannot see this path; use the existing local file when present and create it at that exact path if absent.
